title: Fans | Anaheim Ducks | Anaheim Ducks
text: Wild Wing There are many mascots in sports, but there is only one Wild Wing, the official mascot for the Ducks since the inaugural season in 1993. The first mascot in NHL history to descend onto the ice from the rafters of the arena, he is known for his daredevil stunts and big attitude. The perennial All-Star goalie has made headlines with his exploits, from his play on the ice to starring in action-packed cartoons. Today, you can find this mighty duck riling up Ducks fans and shaking his tail feather at home games or playing hockey with kids around Southern California. Complete the form below to request a Wild Wing appearance at your event. If your requested date is available, an Anaheim Ducks representative will contact you with additional details. Make a request for your event here Follow on Instagram Follow on Twitter/X Follow on TikTok

title: Ducks x Vans Collab | Anaheim Ducks
text: Ducks x Vans Collab Ducks Hall-of-Famer Teemu Selanne designed a special shoe as part of the legendary Ducks x Vans collab, now in its third year! That shoe and a second design will go on sale at the Sunday, February 1 (6:30 p.m.) game vs. Las Vegas (presented by Chick Fil-A) at Honda Center. Shoe quantities are limited, and fans must have a game ticket to shop for them. See below for a special ticket pack for that game! Line will not begin to be queued until 11 a.m. on Sunday, February 1 Customers will be limited to two (2) pairs of shoes per transaction. Whether that be one of each, two Selanne or two checkered. No discounts will be applicable to Vans shoes. Those purchasing between 3 p.m. to 4pm will have the chance to take their purchases back to their vehicles, but any purchases made after 4:30 p.m. will not be allowed to re-enter. Honda Center security will allow Vans shoes to be brought into the arena on this day only. Merchandise (non-shoes) will be available for purchase starting at 4:30 p.m. on the Puck Drop Patio. Some merchandise will be online-exclusive. All merchandise will be available online More Info Get Tickets local_activity Vans Bobbleshoe Ticket Pack Sunday, February 1 • 6:30 p.m. • vs. Vegas Golden Knights Get tickets to the game and its exclusive, in-person merchandise launch through this specific link and you'll also score a limited-edition Teemu Selanne figurine! A 1-Hour Wedding Ceremony or Vow Renewal package includes: One (1) hour access for a non-denominational wedding ceremony or vow renewal in Heritage Hall One (1) hour access to take photos within the TD Garden arena following the ceremony Up to eighteen (18) guests regardless of age. To learn more about applying for a marriage license please visit the City of Boston's website . Additional Details Food and/or beverage is not permitted Outside vendors are limited to one officiant and one photographer Additional furniture, decorations, petals, signs, rice, confetti, balloons, props, or animals are not permitted Attendees must come dressed for the ceremony; on-site holding/prep areas are not available Please complete the form below to be contacted about hosting your wedding or vow renewal at Heritage Hall.

Local businesses and organizations can register to host their own drive and fans are encouraged to help by purchasing a donation from Cradles to Crayons' Amazon Wishlist. title: Official Buffalo Sabres Website | Buffalo Sabres
text: Kim Pegula Owner Kim Pegula is the owner of both the Buffalo Sabres and Buffalo Bills. Kim made history in 2018, when she became the first female president of both an NHL and NFL team. Kim and her husband Terry purchased the Sabres on Feb. 22, 2011 and the AHL’s Rochester Americans later that year, restoring a longtime affiliation between the Sabres and Amerks. On Oct. 8, 2014, Kim and Terry realized a long-time dream when they became only the second owners of the Bills. The Pegulas’ sports ownership also extends to the Buffalo Bandits of the NLL, who have won three league championships under their ownership.Kim has previously served as the co-chair of the NHL’s Executive Inclusion Committee and on the board of directors for the Hockey Hall of Fame. She has also served on the NFL’s Workplace Diversity Committee, committing to ensuring that diversity is a priority in both leagues. Kim’s NFL involvement extended to the league’s Super Bowl and Major Events Advisory Committee, Business Ventures Committee, and NFL Foundation Committee. In 2014, Kim and Terry opened LECOM Harborcenter, a more than $200 million multipurpose facility anchored by two NHL-size ice rinks and a Marriott Hotel franchise. Combined with KeyBank Center, the facility helped attract several major events to Buffalo since its inception, including the NHL Scouting Combine, 2016 NHL Draft, 2018 IIHF World Junior Championships and 2019 NCAA Men’s Frozen Four, as well as a variety of stadium and arena concerts. For their efforts, Kim and Terry have been previously recognized with the Tank Younger Award for embracing diversity in the NFL and their involvement in the Buffalo community landed the Pegulas on the Buffalo Business First Most Influential People list.In addition to their experience in professional sports, Kim and Terry have been committed to the growth of sports at the collegiate level. In 2010, they donated $102 million for the creation of the Pegula Ice Arena at Penn State University. The facility allowed Penn State to create an NCAA Division I hockey program. Terry and Kim also supported Houghton College with a gift of $12 million to build the Kerr-Pegula Athletic Complex, allowing Houghton’s athletic department to become a Division III program.During the COVID-19 pandemic, the Pegulas donated $1.2 million to various relief efforts in Western New York and Kim served on Governor Andrew Cuomo’s Reopening Advisory Board for New York State. Born in Seoul, South Korea on June 7, 1969, Kim was adopted at the age of 5 by Ralph and Marilyn Kerr and moved to Fairport, New York, a suburb of Rochester. She attended nearby Houghton College and graduated in 1991 with a degree in communications. Kim began her professional career with East Resources, Inc. in 1991 and was involved with the company until its sale in 2010.Terry and Kim have five children: Michael, Laura, Jessica, Kelly and Matthew. Jessica competes on the Women’s Tennis Association Tour, currently ranking top 5, and she was a member of the 2021 and 2024 US Olympic Teams.

title: Flames To Host Oilers In Next Gen Showcase Game | Calgary Flames
text: Flames To Host Oilers In Next Gen Showcase Game Flames, Oilers prospects to face off in Calgary on Sept. 14 By Calgary Flames Staff CalgaryFlames.com August 26, 2026 Link copied The Calgary Flames will host the Edmonton Oilers in the Next Gen Showcase game on Monday, September 14 at the Scotiabank Saddledome. Game time is 6:00 p.m. MT with doors opening at 5:00 p.m. MT. Fans will be able to see Matvei Gridin, Arsenii Sergeev, Tyson Gross, Abram Wiebe, Axel Hurtig, as well as other Flames prospects as they face off against their Alberta rival. All tickets for the Next Gen Showcase Game are $10.00 (taxes and fees included) and are available HERE (children two and under are free) with the proceeds going to the Flames Foundation. There will also be an opportunity to donate to the Flames Sports Bank so fans are encouraged to bring new or used sporting equipment. Prior to and during the game, Flames Alumni will be on the concourse signing autographs. Fans can also enjoy interactive games on the concourse, meet Harvey the Hound, purchase 50/50 tickets, and more. text: Since 1994 Four Partners, Three Decades The Calgary Flames have been guided by the same ownership group since 1994 — four Calgary business leaders whose interests span energy, transportation, real estate, and finance, and whose philanthropy has shaped health care, education, and wellness across Alberta. Co-owner since 1994 Role Chairman, CSEC Business Edco Financial Holdings N. Murray Edwards Mr. Edwards became a co-owner of the Calgary Flames in 1994 and is Chairman of Calgary Sports and Entertainment Corporation. He is Owner and Chairman of Edco Financial Holdings Ltd., a merchant banker since 1988, and is a leading investor in, and managing director and chairman of, numerous publicly traded companies including Canadian Natural Resources Limited, and Ensign Energy Services Inc. Mr. Edwards graduated with a Bachelor of Commerce from the University of Saskatchewan with Great Distinction and a Bachelor of Laws with Honours from the University of Toronto. After moving to Calgary in 1983, he became a lawyer and later a Partner with Burnet, Duckworth & Palmer, a Calgary-based law firm. Co-owner since 1994 Role President & CEO, Balmon Investments Honours Officer of the Order of Canada Alvin G. Libin A native Calgarian with business interests in real estate, oil and gas and financial services, Mr. Libin became an owner of the Calgary Flames in 1994. He is the President and Chief Executive Officer of Balmon Investments Ltd., a private management services and investment company. He has a strong commitment to the City of Calgary and to the Province of Alberta and has provided leadership in a wide variety of volunteer positions. In 2003, Mr. Libin and his wife Mona, through The Alvin and Mona Libin Foundation, established The Libin Cardiovascular Institute of Alberta in partnership with the University of Calgary and Alberta Health Services. Its mission is to provide world-class cardiovascular health care, education and research for southern Alberta. He also serves as a director on several corporate and community boards. Mr. Libin is an Officer of the Order of Canada and holds an Honorary Doctors of Laws degree from the University of Calgary. He was inducted into the Alberta Order of Excellence in 2004. Co-owner since 1994 Co-founded Canadian Natural Resources, 1989 Focus Pure North wellness initiative Allan Markin A native Calgarian and longtime philanthropist, Mr. Markin also became an owner of the Calgary Flames hockey club in 1994. Mr. Markin co-founded Canadian Natural Resources Limited (CNRL) in 1989, together with Mr. Edwards. During his tenure as Chairman of CNRL, he was instrumental in growing the company from a small operation of six employees with limited capital to the largest oil and gas producer in Canada. Allan, a fervent advocate for improved health, relinquished his role as Chairman of Canadian Natural Resources Limited in 2012 to devote his efforts to the wellness initiative he established at Pure North. Pure North, an innovative wellness program, focuses on preventing chronic illnesses through personalized nutritional supplements, education, and lifestyle guidance. Having engaged over 46,000 participants, with an emphasis on vulnerable groups, Pure North collaborates with international experts, sharing data with esteemed institutions like the University of Calgary, University of Alberta, Harvard School of Public Health, and others, to educate on optimized nutrition. Additionally, Allan's support extends to initiatives like the APPLE Schools program, promoting healthy habits among students and earning him accolades such as honorary degrees and awards. Central to his philanthropy is elevating education in health and wellness. Co-owner since 1994 Role Chairman, Trimac Transportation Also chairs Flames Foundation for Life Jeffrey J. text: Cashless Payment FAQ The Scotiabank Saddledome will be a cashless venue. All concession stands, retail locations and 50/50 ticket sellers inside Scotiabank Saddledome have contactless terminals that will allow debit, credit, Apple Pay, Google Pay and gift cards as methods of payment. Why have you become a cashless venue? The health and safety of our fans, players and staff is our top priority. Coming out of the Covid-19 pandemic, reducing points of contact including the handling of cash is an important tool to help protect the health and safety for all. In addition, we have listened to feedback from our fans and Season Ticket Members that additional payment options, especially debit cards, is very important. Cashless transactions will allow us to facilitate a wider variety of popular and convenient payment options. Can I still use cash at Scotiabank Saddledome? Cash will no longer be accepted at concession, retail and 50/50 locations inside Scotiabank Saddledome. You will only be able to use your debit card, or credit card, as well as Apple Pay or Google Pay on your mobile device (including smartwatches), at all points of purchase. Scotiabank Saddledome gift cards will also be available to purchase online, to purchase a gift card, please **CLICK HERE** . Which payment methods will be available as part of cashless transactions? Debit cards Credit cards Apply Pay (on your mobile device, including smartwatches) Google Pay (on your mobile device, including smartwatches) Scotiabank Saddledome gift cards Can I bring cash with me and exchange it for a gift card at Scotiabank Saddledome? Gift cards need to be purchased in advance. We are unable to exchange cash for gift cards at Scotiabank Saddledome on game day. To purchase a gift card, please **CLICK HERE** .

text: Championship Parade Info The trophy is coming back to Raleigh, and it's time to celebrate! The Carolina Hurricanes 2026 Championship Celebration presented by Spectrum will feature a parade and rally on Saturday, June 20 , at 11:00 a.m. in Downtown Raleigh . Text CANESPARADE to 888777 to get real-time updates on traffic, weather, and safety for the Championship Celebration. Know Before You Go info Parade Route map Parking & Transportation local_parking Parade Route Saturday's parade will begin at the intersection of Hillsborough and St. Mary's St. and weave through downtown before ending at Davie St. The full map can be viewed below. Following the conclusion of the parade, there will be a rally held at City Plaza, where fans can gather to hear from players, coaches, and special guests. Screens and audio will be placed along Fayetteville St., so those who do not have a spot in City Plaza will be able to watch and hear speeches during the rally. Parking & Transportation Parking: State parking decks will be free to the public on Saturday, which can be viewed here . There will be five other decks offering free parking for the celebration: Cabarrus St. | 436 S. Salisbury St. Moore Square Deck | 233 S. Wilmington St. City Center Deck | 429 S. Wilmington St. City Hall Parking Deck | 201 W. Morgan St. Wilmington St. Station Deck | 117 S. Wilmington St. Additionally, the Performing Arts Center and Convention Center Decks will cost a flat $10. Click here to learn more about parking downtown. Public Transit: To ease congestion, fans are also encouraged to utilize GoRaleigh for transit. The fare is $2.50 for a Day Pass, and riders can pay by cash on the bus or by downloading the UMO app to set up an account and pay via the app. Click here to learn more about transit options in Raleigh. Street Closures: There will be street closures along the entire route of the parade, similar to those closed for the annual Christmas parade. Closures will begin early Saturday morning between 3:30 am and 5:30 am and continue through Saturday afternoon and likely early evening for Fayetteville St. and the adjacent streets within the typical event footprint, such as Hargett, Martin, and Davie. title: Olympic Winter Games | Carolina Hurricanes
text: Watch Live live_tv Full Schedule sports_hockey Stats analytics Bracket leaderboard When Do The Canes Play? Latest News North Carolina's Kayden Beasley To Play For Team USA at Paralympic Winter Games 19-year-old to compete on sled hockey team in Milan Winter Olympics Medalists Return To Raleigh Slavin, United States Win Gold Aho, Finland Take Bronze Tournament Info remove add When will hockey be played during the Winter Olympics? The Olympic Winter Games Milano Cortina 2026 will be held from Feb. 6-22 in Milan, Italy. The Men's Ice Hockey portion of the event begins on Feb. 11 and ends with the Gold Medal Game on Feb. 22. A schedule of games specifically involving Hurricanes players can be found above under "When Do The Canes Play?" A link to the full hockey schedule is also available among the red buttons at the top of the page. remove add Who from the Hurricanes is participating? The Carolina Hurricanes will be well-represented at the Olympic Winter Games, with five players competing: Canada: Seth Jarvis Finland: Sebastian Aho Denmark: Frederik Andersen & Nikolaj Ehlers United States: Jaccob Slavin remove add How can I watch the games? In the U.S., all games can be streamed through Peacock ($) and NBCOlympics.com (with TV provider sign-in). Live and tape-delayed coverage of hockey will be shown on the following TV channels: NBC, CNBC, and USA Network. The full TV listings for hockey can be found on the NBCOlympics.com schedule page by clicking the toggle at the top to “TV Only.” To learn more about watching hockey during the Olympic Winter Games Milano Cortina 2026, click here . remove add What is the hockey tournament format during the Winter Olympics? The 12 teams are broken into three groups and will play a round robin within their group (teams with Hurricanes players in bold ): Group A: Canada, Czechia, France, Switzerland Group B: Italy, Finland, Slovakia, Sweden Group C: Denmark, Germany, Latvia, United States Teams will earn 3 points for a regulation win, 2 points for an OT/SO win and 1 point for an OT/SO loss. After the round robin, the 12 games will be seeded based on the following criteria: Higher position in the group Higher number of points Better goal differential Higher number of goals scored Better 2020 IIHF World Ranking The top four teams receive a bye into the quarterfinals. The teams ranked 5-12 will play in the qualification playoff games with the following matchups: 5 vs 12, 6 vs 11, 7 vs 10, 8 vs 9

title: Grants | Carolina Hurricanes
text: 2026 grant applications are open from march 9 to april 10 The Carolina Hurricanes Foundation strives to meet the health and educational needs of children, with a focus on underserved populations, and to strengthen youth hockey in our community. GRANTS The Carolina Hurricanes Foundation is pleased to support local nonprofits through grant funding. The Foundation accepts grant proposals for grants, awarded at various levels of funding. Priority for grant funding is given to nonprofits that share the Foundation's mission and focus on children's health and education. We appreciate your interest in receiving grant funding from the Carolina Hurricanes Foundation. Please read through the guidelines and restrictions below. To receive grant funding from the Carolina Hurricanes Foundation, organizations must: Be a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt nonprofit organization in good standing with the Internal Revenue Service Share the mission of the Carolina Hurricanes Foundation to strive to meet the health and education needs of children with a focus on impacting underserved populations, and/or strengthening youth hockey in our community Directly serve children in the state of North Carolina with a focus on health or education Be in operation for three or more years Must be available for site visits, provide use of funds summary reports, and recognize the Carolina Hurricanes Foundation as a donor The Carolina Hurricanes Foundation's grant funding does not generally support the following: Event sponsorship or fundraisers, including but not limited to galas, awareness walks, and golf tournaments General operating costs, staff salaries, capital campaigns, endowments, or other reserve funds PTA's, booster clubs, churches, or political organizations If you have any questions or concerns about the grant process, please contact [email protected] . GRANT CYCLES The Carolina Hurricanes Foundation is committed to serving our community in which we live, work and play. The application period is now open and will close on April 10, 2026. Please note, many organizations apply for grants each cycle, and the overall amount of funding requested far exceeds the Carolina Hurricanes Foundation's resources. Declined applications in no way reflect the importance of an organization's mission or programming. Groups that do not receive funding are encouraged to apply again next year and find other creative ways to partner with the Carolina Hurricanes and the Carolina Hurricanes Foundation. Game Changer Grants Grassroots Grants Grants are awarded annually between $10,000 - $20,000 each. Game Changer Grants are designed to help organizations make a significant, programmatic impact in our community. These funds are intended to assist organizations make a positive difference at the grassroots level. Please note: Organizations can only apply for grant funding at one level per grant cycle Click Here To Apply Future Canes Grants Youth Hockey Programs Grants are awarded annually at various levels, based on available funds and the organization's needs. Future Canes Grants are designed to strengthen and grow youth hockey in North Carolina, ensuring that hockey is accessible for everyone. text: NOTE: The 2026 Canes 5K is officially sold out. Get ready to run, walk, cheer, and celebrate like champions to kick off the start of the 2026-27 season with the 13th Annual Canes 5K, presented by UNC Health and assisted by Raleigh Orthopaedic, on Sunday, September 13, 2026, at 8:15 AM! This year's event will feature a 5K course around Lenovo Center and the surrounding areas, two Caniac Kids' Dashes, inflatables, Kona Ice, Travelin’ Tom’s Coffee, a refreshing cool-down zone, appearances from some of your favorite Canes players, and much more. This isn't your average 5K; it's a celebration for the entire Canes community! Whether you're chasing a personal record, taking a victory lap with family and friends, or simply joining the fun, there's something for everyone - including our four-legged Caniacs! Registration Options -SOLD OUT- Registration includes: One (1) ticket to a 2026-27 Canes home game Commemorative t-shirt & sticker Personalized race bib A post-race breakfast, courtesy of US Foods and Lenovo Center staff One (1) cold beer, courtesy of RH Barringer (21+ only) IMPORTANT: Each Canes 5K participant (excluding the Caniac Kids Dash & Full STM participants) will receive one (1) upper-level ticket as part of their registration. There will be a list of predetermined games in the 2026-27 season from which participants can select. Game options will be announced in a post-race email! -SOLD OUT- You must add the promo code sent to your STM account email and your STM account number to receive the discount. Registration includes: Commemorative t-shirt & sticker Personalized race bib A post-race breakfast, courtesy of US Foods and Lenovo Center staff One (1) cold beer, courtesy of RH Barringer (21+ only) IMPORTANT: This registration option is for FULL Season Ticket Members ONLY . You will need to provide your STM account number at check-out. This registration does not include a complimentary game ticket. Refunds will not be issued if the promo code is not applied! -SOLD OUT- Registration includes: Commemorative kids' t-shirt & sticker Personalized race bib Post-race breakfast, courtesy of US Foods and Lenovo Center staff IMPORTANT: This registration does not include a complimentary game ticket. Race Day The 13 th annual Canes 5K presented by UNC Health and assisted by Raleigh Orthopaedic will take place at Lenovo Center on Sunday, Sept. 13, at 8:15 a.m. All proceeds benefit the Carolina Hurricanes Foundation. Participants are strongly encouraged to pick up their packets before race day. One person may pick up multiple participants' packets, but must have a photo of each additional participant's photo ID. text: Parking Lenovo Center offers thousands of designated parking spaces in lots surrounding the building. Arena parking lots open three hours prior to game time. Tailgating is permitted at Lenovo Center. Guests may not use multiple parking spots or restrict access to roadways when tailgating. Please review "Tailgating Rules & Regulations" below for more information. Vehicles must be cleared from the property within one hour of the end of the event unless permitted to stay by Lenovo Center staff, or for safe driving considerations. Any vehicles remaining on the property overnight must be removed by 8:00 a.m. the following day. Season Ticket Members can pre-purchase season parking passes. Contact your rep prior to the start of the season or playoffs for more information. Parking at Lenovo Center is cashless. Fans can prepay for a general parking pass at the time of ticket purchase, or by selecting their event below. Fans can also pay with credit cards on the property (on-site). title: Tommy Hawk | Chicago Blackhawks
text: The official mascot of the Chicago Blackhawks, Tommy Hawk is the NHL's best. This feathery fowl loves to dance, play hockey and generally cause mascot mayhem wherever he goes. Tommy is not only at all Blackhawks home games, but Tommy makes numerous appearances throughout the Chicagoland area and the country. Tommy loves to attend all types of events from birthday parties, block parties, schools, parades, business expos to pretty much anywhere that laughter and fun are needed. Meet Tommy Hawk NAME: Tommy Hawk POSITION: Center (of attention) WEIGHT: Feather weight SHOOTS: T-shirts to the crowd RESIDES: At the United Center HOBBIES: Playing hockey, launching confetti, spraying silly string, dancing, FAVORITE FOODS: Roasted Duck, Pickled Penguin, Coyote Burgers, Buffalo Wings FAVORITE SONGS: Here Come the Hawks, Chelsea Dagger, Shake Your Tail Feather Tommy Hawk Appearances Tommy Hawk is available for booking at events throughout the year, as well as in-arena visits when you're at the United Center for a Blackhawks game! Fill out the form below to request an appearance. Seat Visits Take your gameday to the next level with a special visit from Tommy Hawk! Visits are available in the below packages: Slapshot ($150) : Tommy will spend a timeout visiting your group and taking photos. He will bring a sign, confetti (depending on seat location) and a gift bag for the guest of honor. Hat Trick ($250) : All the same features as the Slapshot, plus a video board message. Love Bird ($175) : Tommy will help you take your proposal to the next level by visiting your seat and helping you ask that special someone to marry you. External Appearances Tommy Hawk is available for requests to appear at public and private events throughout the year! Based on availability, Tommy can add fun mascot antics at a school assembly, grand opening, or other special event. Goal Horn Experience Up to six fans have the opportunity to get a one of a kind pregame experience. Fans will be able to watch the pregame Goal Horn moment occur live in person. Following the goal horn moment Tommy Hawk will pose for photos with the group and provide gift bags to Goal Horn Experience guests. Cost: $500 (up to six fans) Tommy Hawk Teamwork Timeout This highly interactive assembly focuses on teamwork and uses Character Counts as the basis of being a good teammate. Tommy Hawk and his emcee will get the students laughing and having fun, while teaching the important life lessons of working together as a team. This engaging assembly runs approximately 30-45 minutes and will have students and faculty laughing out loud. The positive message will impact students beyond the classroom and have them wanting to work together as a team to accomplish goals. For further information, contact Joseph Doyle at [email protected]

text: PRESS BOX HOME home MEDIA POLICIES policy CREDENTIAL REQUESTS mail FOLLOW @BLUEJACKETSPR web STAFF DIRECTORY reorder PRONUNCIATION GUIDE headphones ROSTER groups TEAM STATS menu MEDIA POLICIES MEDIA CREDENTIALS Credentials will be required for all games. Requests for Individual Game Passes will be issued on a priority basis to media on specific assignments. Such requests should be submitted in writing to Jack Weller at [email protected] no later than 12 p.m. the day before a home game. Photo identification will be required when picking up credentials, which must be visibly worn at all times. Local media interested in credentials for Blue Jackets road games must submit their requests to Jack Weller at [email protected] by 12 p.m. ET two days prior to the road game. MEDIA ENTRANCE/CREDENTIAL PICKUP Practices & Morning Skates: Media covering practices, including game day morning skates, can enter Nationwide Arena through 24-Hour Security beginning one hour before the scheduled practice time... Game Nights: Credentials can be picked up at the Box Office entrance, located on the southwest side of Nationwide Arena near Tim Hortons, beginning two and a half hours prior to game time. MEDIA PARKING Practices: Media parking is available in the Nationwide Arena Garage, attached to the north side of the building and accessible from Neil Ave. Please bring your ticket to be validated. Morning Skates: Media parking is available in the Nationwide Arena Garage, attached to the north side of the building. Media must download a digital pass to access the garage on game days. Game Nights: Media parking is available at the Front Street Garage, located at 285 N Front St., for a reduced charge of $5 per vehicle. All game day media parking is automated. Please contact Glenn Odebralski at [email protected] for instructions and a required code for parking. PRESS ELEVATORS The press elevators, located just inside the Nationwide Arena Box Office, will be available for use by members of the media for all practices and games. Access will be restricted to event level (lobby only), main concourse and press level. PRESS BOX The press box is located above sections 213-219 on the south/southeast side of Nationwide Arena. An elevator is located near the ticket office. Private booths are assigned for NHL off-ice officials (PL023), video replay officials (PL027), home TV (PL019) and radio (PL018), visiting TV (PL020) and radio (PL021), as well as visiting team management (PL022). DINING FACILITIES The Press Lounge is located on the event level of Nationwide Arena, near the Zamboni entrance. Please show your credential to the attendant for entrance. Meals will be served prior to all home games. The cost is $11.75 per person (plus tax) and all transactions are credit card only (cashless). PRACTICE AND GAME DAY INTERVIEWS If the team holds a practice or morning skate, players and Head Coach Dean Evason will be available at its conclusion with players available in the Blue Jackets' locker room and Evason available in the press conference room, located on event level just down from the dressing room. POST-GAME INTERVIEWS The team’s dressing room will be open to the media five minutes after the game’s conclusion. Blue Jackets Head Coach Dean Evason will meet the media in the press conference room approximately 20 minutes after each contest. WIRELESS SERVICE Complimentary wireless internet is available in the arena by selecting the following in your web browser: WAP: NWArenaWiFi (No password required). PHOTOGRAPHY Requests for photo credentials will be handled the same way as media passes. Photo positions are limited and will be assigned for each game. Photographers must comply with assignments and shooting regulations established by the Blue Jackets and the NHL and shoot from designated areas only. Photographers requiring additional information, including equipment and strobe rental, should contact Glenn Odebralski at 614/246-0288 or Team Photographer Kirk Irwin at 720/

title: Toy Drive | Columbus Blue Jackets
text: Every child deserves a toy at the holidays. Unfortunately, not every family can provide that holiday cheer. The Columbus Blue Jackets are asking fans to support The Salvation Army of Central Ohio's efforts to brighten the holidays for local families in need. The Salvation Army operates central Ohio's largest holiday toy and food distribution program. They provide food and toys to nearly 8,000 families over a two-day period. Christmas Cheer provides a true holiday experience for families that may need a little help this time of year. The toy drive gives that program a big boost by offering the 5th Line a chance to provide the toys the Salvation Army will give away in its Christmas Cheer program in mid-December. How To Donate Fans coming to the December 4th game against the Detroit Red Wings are encouraged to bring a new, unwrapped toy. Before the game, toys will be accepted by volunteers outside the arena entrances. Fans who donate that night will receive a voucher redeemable for a buy one get one ticket offer. (Offer limited to one per household) If fans are not able to join us for the game they can drop off toys from November 17 to December 12 at any OhioHealth Chiller Ice Rink located in Easton, Dublin, and North or at the Blue Line stores located at Nationwide Arena and Polaris Fashion Place.

title: Amazon Prime | Dallas Stars
text: shop Google Play apple App Store Fans with an Amazon Prime membership can watch all non-nationally televised games within the Dallas Stars regional territory (Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana, Arkansas) on Prime Video with no additional subscription required. The only games that won’t be available on Amazon Prime will be the 13 Stars games selected for national broadcasts on ESPN, ABC, TNT, or ESPN+/Hulu. Stars broadcasts will continue to feature the dynamic duo of color analyst Daryl “Razor” Reaugh and play-by-play announcer Josh Bogorad . Brien Rea and Brent Severyn return to provide comprehensive coverage on pregame, intermission and postgame shows. Enter your zip/postal code below to see what team(s) are in your broadcast area. Fans can find a full list of teams and local broadcast stations here . Broadcast Team Daryl "Razor" Reaugh TV/Radio Color Analyst Daryl Reaugh is in his 30th season on Stars television and radio broadcasts and his 28th as the team’s color analyst. For two seasons from 2016-18, Reaugh had served as the team’s play-by-play announcer in the wake of Dave Strader’s cancer diagnosis. During the 2025 offseason, Reaugh was named the recipient of the Foster Hewitt Memorial Award, which is awarded annually to the member of the radio and television industry who made outstanding contributions to their profession and the game during their career in hockey broadcasting as decided by the NHL Broadcasters’ Association. Reaugh came to Dallas from the Hartford Whalers, where he served as the color analyst on SportsChannel New England’s telecasts during the 1995-96 campaign. He has also demonstrated his expertise on the national stage, having worked with Versus, NBC Sports Network, ABC, ESPN, FOX and CBC’s Hockey Night in Canada. Josh Bogorad TV/Radio Play-By-Play Announcer Josh Bogorad is in his 14th season with the Stars broadcast team, and his eighth as the team’s play-by-play broadcaster. Prior to his current role, he served as the host of Stars Live, the pregame, intermission and postgame show during Stars broadcasts on FOX Sports Southwest. Bogorad joined the Stars in 2013 as the pregame, intermission and postgame radio host on The Ticket. Since becoming the Stars’ play-by-play broadcaster, Bogorad was voted the 2020 Texas Sportscaster of the Year by the National Sports Media Association and won the 2022 Lone Star Sports EMMY in the Play-by-Play category. Brien Rea TV Analyst Brien Rea is in his ninth season with the Stars broadcast team and returns to the host role after spending the previous three as a television analyst. He spent his first three seasons as the host of Stars Live from 2018-21. In 2023, Rea won two Lone Star Emmy awards for Sports Program - Live (Jamie Benn’s 1,000th game) and Anchor - Sports Program. He won his first Lone Star Emmy in 2021 for Sports Program - Live (Stars Live - Return To The Stanley Cup Final). Prior to joining the Stars broadcast team, Rea spent four seasons as the play-by-play announcer for the Texas Stars, Dallas’ development affiliate in the American Hockey League. In addition to his broadcasting duties, he also served as director of broadcasting and media relations for Texas and oversaw the team’s public relations efforts. Brent Severyn TV Analyst Brent Severyn is in his 23rd season as an analyst for the Dallas Stars broadcast. A native of Vegreville, Alberta, Severyn has a diverse hockey background. A seven-year NHL veteran with 13 years of professional hockey experience, he has played at many levels since leaving his hometown. They include the Western Hockey League, Canadian University, American Hockey League and the DEL in Germany. Originally selected by the Winnipeg Jets in the fifth round of the 1984 NHL Draft, Severyn was an all-star at the Canadian University level and a first team all-star in the AHL. title: StarCenter | Dallas Stars Adaptive Sports | Dallas Stars
text: sports_hockey Adaptive Hockey sports_hockey Sled Hockey sports_hockey Warrior Hockey Dallas Stars Adaptive Sports provides adaptive ice hockey programs for athletes of all abilities, including those with intellectual, emotional, and physical disabilities. Dallas Stars Adaptive Sports is proud to join the hundreds of teams and thousands of athletes that participate in adaptive hockey programs nationwide, ranging from Learn-to-Plays to weekly/monthly practices and games and regional and national tournaments/events. Adaptive hockey provides a supportive environment for athletes of different abilities to play the game, learn sportsmanship and teamwork, and build friendships and community. Dallas Stars Adaptive Sports is a member of the American Special Hockey Association and USA Hockey. To learn more, you can visit their websites at: www.specialhockey.org and www.usahockey.com/specialhockey For more information or questions on how to get started, please contact [email protected] . ADAPTIVE SPECIALTY PROGRAMS ADAPTIVE HOCKEY Our Adaptive Hockey discipline provides hockey opportunities for athletes with intellectual, developmental, and physical disabilities, enabling them to play the game, learn sportsmanship and teamwork, and build friendships and community. Our programs are staffed by experienced coaches and supported by volunteers who offer peer-to-peer encouragement and support to our athletes. Rookies Registration SLED HOCKEY The premise of the game is exactly the same as ice hockey with a few equipment modifications. Instead of skating on two legs, the player sits in a seat mounted onto a tubular frame with two skates blades mounted directly underneath the seat. To propel us on the ice, we use two modified hockey sticks with metal picks on the bottom to push us across the ice. We are always looking to introduce new people to the sport and our team. Rookies Registration WARRIOR HOCKEY The Dallas Stars Warrior program is dedicated to empowering disabled individuals and veterans through the transformative power of hockey. Our mission is to provide a supportive and inclusive environment where players can build physical and mental strength, develop teamwork and camaraderie, and achieve personal and athletic goals. We are committed to honoring and serving those who have made sacrifices for our country, and to helping them thrive both on and off the ice. PROUD PARTNERS AND CORPORATE SPONSORS Previous Next

title: Fans | Detroit Red Wings | Detroit Red Wings
text: Detroit Red Wings Drumline Apply Now Questions? Ahead of the 2024-25 Detroit Red Wings season, we are excited to announce the audition process for the Red Wings Drumline. After another exciting season as part of the soundtrack in Hockeytown, the Red Wings Drumline will continue to be a fixture at Wings home games, community and special events in metro Detroit year-round. We're looking for talented drummers who perform both physically as well as musically and demonstrate an outgoing personality that will entertain and engage the best fans in hockey. Please keep this in mind as you prepare for your audition. If interested, submit all required information as outlined below. Virtual Audition Record an audition video adhering to the instructions below: Video must include the following exercises: "Roll Exercise" - Three reps (1st at 156, 2nd at 188 & 3rd at 212) TA 22" - Two reps (1st at 120 & 2nd at 136) Red Wings Drumline Audition Piece (sheet music can be found here ) Applicant's Choice - Perform a selection of your choosing that you feel best represents your abilities and what you can bring to the Red Wings Drumline Your video should be framed to include your entire drum/cymbals, upper body and face. Final video should be uploaded to Vimeo or YouTube, with a working unlisted URL to be included in the application below. Applications will be accepted through 5pm on Wednesday, August 21. If you have any questions, please email [email protected] . The Detroit Red Wings Game Presentation team will review all applications as they’re submitted. Candidates that are selected to move forward to the audition phase will receive a formal invitation from a DRW Game Presentation member and/or the DRW Drumline Director no later than Friday, August 23. title: Oilers+ Frequently Asked Questions | Edmonton Oilers
text: Frequently Asked Questions remove add WHAT IS OILERS+? Oilers+ is a digital streaming service. This service will give fans exclusive access to behind-the-scenes content, live shows, a post-game show and the most insightful Oilers analysis available. Oilers+ is available 24/7, 365 days a year in nearly all countries in the world. remove add WHAT DOES OILERS+ OFFER? Live and on-demand videos, contests, and digital rewards. remove add WHAT CAN I WATCH ON OILERS+? The new year-round, all-access show titled "The Drop" as well as live pre-season games, rookie camp games, training camp scrimmages, live post-game shows for all regular season games, practice reports, game cutdowns, highlights and insightful analysis from Oilers TV talent. Oilers+ is a destination for the entire family. The platform will also feature hockey-themed lifestyle content from around Ice District with fitness, food, and family features. Kids can also learn hockey skills from acclaimed Oilers alumni. remove add WHAT HISTORICAL CONTENT IS ON OILERS+? Oilers+ has a number of historical and recent-history shows for all fans. While this library is always growing, Oilers+ will feature full seasons of Oil Change, retirement ceremonies, the building of Rogers Place, Stanley Cup team reunions, and much more. Oilers+ will also feature hundreds of hours of historical game footage, behind-the-scenes clips, and insights to life on the road. remove add WHAT IS LIFESTYLE CONTENT? Oilers+ is for the fans. This service will round out the customer experience with hockey workouts, yoga, and the best cuisine and mixology across ICE District. Application Features remove add WHAT ARE THE FEATURES OF OILERS+ AND WHERE ARE THEY OFFERED? Live and on-demand videos for subscribers. Everything is global except for a very few select countries. Cost Device Support remove add HOW MUCH DOES OILERS+ COST? To view Oilers+ subscription pricing options in your area, please create or log in to your Oilers+ Account and click on "Subscriptions" under "My Account." remove add WHAT DEVICES CAN I STREAM OILERS+ ON? Oilers+ is available on devices running the following platforms: Web browsers (PC and mobile) Apple (iOS phone, iOS tablet) Apple TV Android (phones, tablets) Android TV Amazon Fire TV Chromecast remove add WHAT DEVICES CAN I INTERACT WITH THE APP? Contests and rewards are only available on our custom mobile applications on Apple's iOS and Google's Android operating systems. We recommend running the latest version of each operating system for the optimal streaming experience. remove add ARE LIVE GAMES STREAMED ON OILERS+? Select pre-season games will be streamed live on Oilers+. The Oilers media rights partner, Sportsnet, will broadcast and stream all regular season and Oilers playoff games. Check your local listings for access to live Oilers games. remove add HOW DO GAMES GET ADDED TO OILERS+? Special features, game cutdowns and highlights will be made available for streaming 48 hours after the conclusion of the live game. Oilers+ will not stream live or replay regular season games. Special features and other all-access shows will be made available as soon as possible. remove add IN WHICH COUNTRIES IS OILERS+ AVAILABLE? Oilers+ is available worldwide except for regions such as the Crimea Region, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, and Financial Action Task Force restricted jurisdictions (such as Russia). Subscription Management remove add HOW DO I CANCEL MY SUBSCRIPTION? On your web browser: Click on the "My Subscriptions" tab under "My Account". Click "Cancel Subscription" and when asked to confirm click "Yes, Cancel Subscription." remove add HOW DO I RESUME MY SUBSCRIPTION? You can resume access to Oilers+ at any time as long as your payment information is up-to-date by logging in to your Oilers+ Account on your web browser or app, going to "Subscriptions" under "Account" and selecting "Restore Purchase." Your Account remove add HOW DO I CHANGE MY ACCOUNT INFORMATION? To update your account

title: Fan Requests | Edmonton Oilers
text: Fan Requests REGISTERED CHARITIES If your organization is a registered charity, more information on how to apply for funding and/or a donation through the Edmonton Oilers Community Foundation (EOCF) can be found here . DONATION REQUESTS The Edmonton Oilers support non-charitable organizations via in-kind donations. These contributions include autographed Oilers memorabilia, including sticks, hats, pucks and photographs. Our primary focus is minor hockey and ringette fundraising initiatives within Oil Country first and foremost. However, we do our best to fulfill requests from other community groups and fundraising efforts. All requests must be received at least six weeks prior to the event in order to qualify for consideration. Faxed requests, emails and phone calls will not be accepted. Only requests completed via the online process will be considered. To submit a donation request for review, please click here . Every request will be responded to in a timely manner. Due to the high volume of requests received, we regret that we cannot fulfill every request. We please ask that you do not call to check on the status of your request. PERSONAL ITEMS & MERCHANDISE The Edmonton Oilers Hockey Club will not accept any personal items to be autographed by our players, alumni or coaches. These items are important to you and we want to prevent the misfortune of damaged or misplaced items. Please note that any item sent to the organization will be immediately returned unsigned. FAN MAIL Edmonton Oilers players receive hundreds of letters from fans and each player attempts to respond in a timely manner. If there is an individual you would like to send mail to, please send to the address below and it will be passed along to the player. We recommend that you do not send any items of value or importance. The Edmonton Oilers cannot guarantee that all letters will be responded to or the safe return of these items. Edmonton Oilers Hockey Club ATTN: [PLAYER NAME] 300, 10214 - 104 Avenue NW Edmonton, AB T5J 0H6

title: Fans | Florida Panthers | Florida Panthers
text: Where is Sunrise, Florida? The Florida Panthers play their home games at Amerant Bank Arena in Sunrise, Florida. Sunrise is a town just west of Ft. Lauderdale and just north of Miami. A part of Broward County , Sunrise is conveniently located at the center of Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach counties. It is also easily accessible via 595, 75, 95 and the Sawgrass Expressway. Click here for directions to Amerant Bank Arena . Click here for what Broward County has to offer. Sunrise, Florida Is... 7.2 Miles from Coral Springs, FL 13 Miles from Ft. Lauderdale Beach 14 Miles from Ft. Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport 16.02 Miles from Boca Raton, FL 34 Miles from South Beach, Miami 40 Miles from West Palm Beach, FL 53.9 Miles from Palm Beach, FL 96.7 Miles from Naples, FL 181 Miles from Key West (Southernmost point of US) 198 Miles from the Kennedy Space Center 215 Miles from Cinderella's Castle 1,068 Miles from New York City 1,388 Miles from Montreal, Canada 1,489 Miles from Minneapolis, Minnesota 4,879 Miles from North Pole, Alaska 5,085 Miles from Tampere, Finland (Aleksander Barkov's hometown) Sunrise Facts Sunrise was originally known as Sunrise Golf Village, and was incorporated in 1961 by Norman Johnson. Johnson was appointed mayor by Governor Farris Bryant even though at that point, there were no residents in the village. Norman Johnson used the "Upside Down House" as a way to attracted buyers to the area. The name, Sunrise Golf Village was shortened to the more succinct Sunrise in 1971. Sunrise has the distinct honor of having Florida's first Ikea. Sawgrass Mills Mall is the 7th largest mall in the US (2,383,906 sq. ft.) and also the largest single story mall in the US. The Mall is also kind of shaped like an alligator which is very fitting considering Sunrise's proximity to the Everglades. Sunrise hosts a number of special events every year including the Harvest Festival every October and a 'Woodstock' event in December. The annual Sunrise Fourth of July Celebration is hosted at Amerant Bank Arena and features live music and fireworks.

text: #16 Aleksander Barkov How Acquired: Selected by Florida in the 1st Round (2nd overall) of the 2013 NHL Draft 2025 Playoffs: 2025 Stanley Cup Champion with Florida, posting a team-leading 16 assists in 23 games. Amassed five points (0-5-5) in six Stanley Cup Final games vs. EDM Tied for points lead (7) in 2025 Eastern Conference Final Amassed three points (2-1-3) in Eastern Conference Final Game 3, May 24 vs. CAR Buried a goal in Eastern Conference Final Game 2, May 22 at CAR Dished two assists in Round 2, Game 7, May 18 at TOR Produced a three-game point streak (2-1-3) from Round 2, Game 2 to Round 2, Game 4 vs. TOR Amassed five points (1-4-5) in the 2025 Round 1 vs. TBL Scored goal (1-0-1) in Round 1, Game 5, April 30 at TBL Tallied two points (0-2-2) in Round 1, Game 1, April 22 at TBL PLAYOFF HIGHLIGHTS Franchise leader in playoff games (94), assists (552) and points (863) Tied for the team lead in points during the 2024 postseason with a career high eight goals, 14 assists and 22 points (8-14-22). He also led all Cats forwards in faceoff win percentage (55.2) Led Florida with seven power-play points (1-6-7) and four game-winning goals in the 2024 postseason Logged a team-high eight points (3-5-8) vs. BOS in Round 2 of 2024 playoffs, including a postseason-career high four points (2-2-4) in Game 2 and two game-winning goals (Games 2 and 4) Posted five points (2-3-5) over the five-game Round 1 series vs. TBL in 2024 playoffs, including a shorthanded goal and 3 points (2-1-3) in Game 5 to clinch series Recorded 16 points (5-11-16) in 21 games in Florida’s Cup Final run in 2022-23, tying for second-most takeaways (24) of any skater in the 2023 postseason Posted seven points (2-5-7) in 10 games against WSH and TBL in 2021-22 Recorded seven points (1-6-7) in six games against TBL in 2020-21, including two multi-point outings Registered four points (1-3-4) over four games with Florida in 2020 Stanley Cup Qualifier Appeared in six playoff games with Florida in 2015-16, notching three points (2-1-3) against NYI CAREER HIGHLIGHTS Missed entire 2025-26 season due to injury 2024-25 Frank J. Selke Trophy & King Clancy Memorial Trophy winner Captained Finland at the 2025 Four Nations Face Off Became the first Finnish-born NHL player to win the Stanley Cup as captain Won his second career Frank J. Selke Trophy (also: 2020-21) as the NHL’s best defensive forward. He became the seventh player in NHL history to win the Selke and win the Stanley Cup in the same season. Notched his 416th assist, surpassing J. Huberdeau for Florida all-time assists record, Jan. 2, 2024 at ARI Barkov is the 10th captain in Panthers history, and holds the club records for games played, goals, assists, points and power-play goals in the regular season 2018-19 Lady Byng Trophy winner, finalist in 2015-16 and 2017-18. He was the youngest European-born recipient of Lady Byng Memorial Trophy (2018-19) Played in 2018 and 2023 NHL All-Star Game Recorded 16 points (5-11-16) in 21 games in Florida’s Cup Final run in 2022-23, tying for second-most takeaways (24) of any skater in the 2023 postseason Posted seven points (2-5-7) in 10 games against WSH and TBL in 2021-22 Recorded seven points (1-6-7) in six games against TBL in 2020-21, including two multi-point outings Registered four points (1-3-4) over four games with Florida in 2020 Stanley Cup Qualifier Appeared in six playoff games with Florida in 2015-16, notching three points (2-1-3) against NYI Recorded 78 points (23-55-78) over 68 games while pacing the Cats in takeaways (56) and faceoff win percentage (54.9) in 2022-23 Surpassed J. Huberdeau's franchise points record (614) on March 20, 2023 at DET Recorded 158th multi-point game, most in club history on March 4, 2023 vs. PIT Logged a career-high 11-game point streak (5-12-17) from Jan. 10-28, 2023 Scored his 67th career PPG to surpass S. title: Nordy | Minnesota Wild
text: A WILD animal born in the north woods of the Iron Range, Nordy was found skating the frozen lakes and ponds near Eveleth, MN. While no one truly knew what sort of Wild animal he is, it was clear that Nordy encompassed the true spirit of the Wild. So in 2008, Nordy proudly accepted the offer to become the mascot for the Minnesota Wild. He stays true to his "up north-y" roots but has moved into his own lair at Grand Casino Arena so he can be closer to his favorite hockey team. Nordy lives for hockey and is one of the last players to still sport his "hockey hair" mullet. Nordy is strong and rugged but huggable and fun loving. He loves to visit fans and get high fives but be careful...he has been known to have a bit of a Wild side too. Twitter Instagram

Certain restrictions apply. Learn more about how your child can be a part of this iconic tradition! Learn More Enter Now

text: Each season, the Minnesota Wild partners with local organizations to be the beneficiaries of fan-supported community drives. These drives include food, clothing, school supplies and more. Be sure to check back often to see how you can help create a greater State of Hockey! Used Hockey Equipment Drive The Minnesota Wild, Let’s Play Hockey and Minnesota Hockey are teaming up for the annual Used Hockey Equipment Drive. Fans are encouraged to donate new or gently used hockey gear at participating rinks across the Twin Cities, with goalie equipment, sticks and helmets especially needed. Thousands of donated items will be distributed free to local hockey associations and individuals at Grand Casino Arena on Oct. 11, helping more players across the State of Hockey get the gear they need to play. text: El Jefe Radio Alex Martinez Radio Play-by-Play Alex Martinez is the current Spanish play-by-play radio announcer for the Nashville Predators on El Jefe Radio. Martinez was born and raised in Tegucigalpa, Honduras, where he was inspired by his father’s work in the radio industry. Martinez graduated from the National Autonomous University of Honduras (UNAH) in 1993 with a degree in Journalism, which he used to jumpstart his career on the Honduran radio station, Stereo Mil. In 2000, Martinez moved to Nashville, Tennessee and began Spanish radio sports programs on Latina 900AM and La Sabrosita 810AM. He went on to start the program, Deportivo al Aire, the first Spanish-language radio sports show in the city. Martinez joined El Jefe in 2017, where he covered the budding new Nashville SC professional soccer franchise, continuing coverage of the team as it moved to the MLS in 2020. Starting in 2022, Martinez began covering Nashville Predators games, serving as the Spanish play-by-play voice that continues to bring the story of the Smashville and the NHL to the local community. Nayele Alamilla Radio Play-by-Play Nayele Alamilla is a Smashville native with a passion for radio and sports! She earned her Bachelor’s degree at MTSU in 2016, majoring in Multimedia Journalism. By turning her curiosity into captivating stories, playing listeners’ favorite songs on the radio, being a morning show co-host, and pursuing her love for sports, she has carved a path as the first Latina woman to do sports broadcasting on Spanish radio in Nashville. With 9 years of experience in radio sports broadcasting, from soccer to hockey, Nayele continues to follow her passion for sports one broadcast at a time. Jordi Sánchez Radio Anaylst Born on May 1st, 1978, in the city of Celaya, Guanajuato, Mexico, Jorge "Jordi" Sánchez showed an interest in sports from a young age, not only participating in them but also from a journalism perspective, as he used to write his own articles at home with a typewriter and clippings from sports publications. Nacido el 1° de mayo de 1978 en la ciudad de Celaya, Guanajuato, México, Jorge "Jordi" Sánchez mostró interés en los deportes desde pequeño, no sólo practicándolos sino también desde la perspectiva del periodismo ya que solía hacer sus propios artículos en casa, con una máquina de escribir y recortes de publicaciones deportivas. Read More During his adolescence and early adulthood, he was also very drawn to the arts, such as writing and music, which led him to venture into the local music scene with different music bands. This also allowed him to get involved in the radio as a host of a weekly program called "Proyecto Indie," which showcased local musical proposals. Currently, he is the communications specialist for a plastic injection company. He has participated in some local radio and television programs on sports topics, and since 2019, realizing the lack of Spanish-language content about NHL hockey, a sport he has followed and been passionate about for over 30 years, he decided to launch his own content channel on YouTube called "Hockey en Español" to promote this sport among Spanish-speaking audiences. This hockey channel has become the most prolific in the Spanish language during its existence, with nearly 200 videos available to date. It was like this that Alexis Martínez and El Jefe reached out to him to extend an invitation to participate as an analyst in the Nashville Predators radio broadcasts for the Spanish-speaking audience, which he gladly accepted. This marked the most significant milestone for him as a professional. A couple of years later, the broadcast team of El Jefe Deportes, covering the Predators hockey games, has grown in experience and involvement with the team and its impact on its fans, aiming to deliver a professional, high-quality product filled with passion—the same passion that characterizes Latino spirit now fused with the ice of the Bridgestone Arena and the sound of blades, sticks, pucks,

text: Music City Hockey In Smashville: An Animated Program Link copied Video Link Copied Overview Watch Party How to Watch Overview Get ready, Preds fans! We’re teaming up with NewsChannel 5 to bring you a one-of-a-kind animated broadcast experience presented by Monroe Carell Jr. Children’s Hospital at Vanderbilt. Welcome to the Hockeyverse! Tune-in to NewsChannel 5 at 6 PM on April 1st as we take you inside Music City Hockey in Smashville, a fully animated experience featuring your favorite Preds players, Gnash, and all his friends as the Preds take on the Columbus Blue Jackets. This special animated program is packed with fun hockey facts, exclusive player interviews, special features, and a unique look into our home in Music City, making it a great experience for families and fans of all ages. This is sure to be an animated adventure like no other! Read More Watch Party The Factory at Franklin Tuesday, April 1 | 5:00 PM Hosted by Wayne D and DJ Battle Join us for a special Preds Animated Program Watch Party event on Tuesday, April 1 st at the Factory at Franklin! Bring the whole family for games, giveaways, a guest appearance from Gnash, and more. The party starts at 5pm so arrive early to enjoy the fun. HOW TO WATCH AT HOME Date: Tuesday, April 1 Time: 6 p.m. CT How To Watch: NewChannel 5 (WTVF) and NHL.com NHL.com Previous Next 'Music City Hockey in Smashville' Animated Program Set to Present the Preds Like Never Before NHL, NewsChannel 5 Will Broadcast Predators, Blue Jackets Game on April 1 in Unique Animated Form You’ve never seen the Predators like this before. On April 1, when the team faces the Blue Jackets in Columbus, fans back in Nashville will have the opportunity to watch their favorite club in a way that is, quite simply, incredibly cool. In conjunction with the NHL and NewsChannel 5 (WTVF), the Predators will be part of a unique initiative with a broadcast of the data visualization entitled, “Music City Hockey in Smashville” presented by Monroe Carell Jr. Children’s Hospital at Vanderbilt at 6 p.m. CT on April 1. Airing on NewsChannel 5, the CBS affiliate in Nashville, fans will be treated to an animated broadcast of not only the game between the Preds and Blue Jackets, but also an adventure with team mascot GNASH with his Music City friends to watch a Predators hockey game. Predators broadcasters Max Herz and Chris Mason - who have also been animated - will call the game live as it happens on NewsChannel 5, and the broadcast will then be available on YouTube shortly after the contest. All in all, this is something not only young Preds fans - but the entire family - won’t want to miss. “I'm just happy everyone else gets to see it, because I've been describing it to people, and words can't do it justice,” Herz said. “The art, the animation, the renderings of Nashville, the different things they can do with the technology, are unbelievable… They’ve done such a great job making this a totally unique thing. I just want everyone to see it, because once people see it, they're going to get glued to it and want to keep watching.” It's going to be a party 🕺 Experience a brand-new side of Smashville in a fully-animated program on April 1 as we take on the Blue Jackets! More on how to watch: https://t.co/rgILj2ZpXv pic.twitter.com/TMk6gKtpp6 — Nashville Predators (@PredsNHL) March 25, 2025 “We're very excited on a number of fronts,” NHL SVP of Marketing & Innovation Casey Hall said. “It's exciting to us to see the technology that we have so heavily invested in and developed over the last number of years begin to come to life, and to come to life in different ways. See you at The Garden! remove add Where can I find the Kith for Rangers collection pop-up store? The Kith for Rangers collection will be available for purchase at our pop-up store in Chase Square. Chase Square is located in the main entrance of Madison Square Garden on 7th Avenue between 31st Street and 33rd Street. You do not need a wristband, appointment, or game ticket to access the pop-up. remove add How can I access the pop-up store? Simply enter Chase Square, located in Madison Square Garden at 7th Avenue and 32nd Street. The pop-up is located past the security area. You may only visit the store at the listed hours, below. You may not line -up outside of stated store hours. You do not need a wristband, appointment, or game ticket to access the pop-up. remove add What are the dates and hours of the pop-up? The Kith for Rangers pop-up will open on Monday, December 15 and will remain open for all Rangers home games throughout December. The store will open at 5:00 PM ET and can be accessed on a first-come, first-served basis. You may arrive beginning at 4:00 PM ET. Guests are not permitted to line up earlier than 4:00 PM ET nor can guests "hold" a place in line for others who are arriving later. remove add Can I return my purchase? No, all sales are final. For answers to more questions, please contact us at 212-465-6225 , Monday through Friday between 9:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. ET, and Saturday and Sunday between 10:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. ET or via email at [email protected] . New York Rangers vs. Anaheim Ducks The Kith for the New York Rangers Collection will be available for purchase in-arena on December 15 when the Blueshirts face off against the Ducks. Intermission performances consist of two musical sets, preferably with a medley of songs. Set 1: First Intermission – 9:00 approximate length Set 2: Second Intermission – 11:00 approximate length Short segments of each song tend to do the best with the audience given the limited time. remove add What time do acts load in? 1:30pm is the standard load in time for a 7:00pm game time. remove add Where do acts perform? How big is the surface? Acts perform on the Hard Rock Ottawa Stage in section 213. The stage is 20’ wideand 38’ deep, but only the front 9’ is open above into the arena. title: Official Philadelphia Flyers Website | Philadelphia Flyers
text: Fan Code of Conduct The National Hockey League and its Member Clubs are committed to creating a safe and comfortable environment and enjoyable entertainment experience. NHL fans have a right to expect an environment in which they will be treated in a consistent, professional and courteous manner by all arena, team and League personnel. The Players and Officials have the same rights. Accordingly, fans are responsible for their own conduct. The following standards have been established with respect to fan conduct: Fans are entitled to enjoy the hockey experience free from disruptive or inconsiderate behaviors or unruly actions. Fans may not interfere with the event and/or athletes in any manner. Fans shall refrain from using abusive language or obscene gestures. Fans may not engage in fighting, throwing objects or other behavior deemed detrimental to the experience of other guests and those who engage in any of these actions will immediately be ejected from the game. Fans are encouraged to report inappropriate behavior to arena staff. Fans who choose to consume alcohol must do so in a legal and responsible manner. Intervention with an intoxicated or impaired fan will be handled in a prompt and safe manner. Fans shall comply with requests from arena staff regarding arena operational and emergency procedures. Fans may not engage in unauthorized commercial activity while on arena property. Violation of the Fan Code of Conduct may result in eviction from the arena without a ticket refund. The NHL and its Member Clubs thank you for adhering to the provisions of the NHL Fan Code of Conduct.

title: Sleepers No More | Philadelphia Flyers
text: Sleepers No More Travis Konecny, Travis Sanheim and Rasmus Ristolainen have all been in Philadelphia for quite some time. But the improvement in the play of all three of them has been the highlight of the season so far for the Flyers. By Brian Smith philadelphiaflyers.com December 05, 2024 Link copied Travis Konecny, Travis Sanheim and Rasmus Ristolainen have all been in Philadelphia for quite some time. Konecny is even a two-time All-Star. But the improvement in the play of all three of them has been the highlight of the season so far for the Flyers, of course along with the arrival of Matvei Michkov. That has not gone unnoticed, as demonstrated Wednesday when the Travii were named to Team Canada’s Four Nations roster, while Ristolainen was selected to Team Finland. The latter’s inclusion was expected; the two former, not so much. Konecny was mentioned by a couple pundits this summer as perhaps knocking on the door for a spot; Sanheim doesn’t seem to have been on anyone’s radar. But they have played their way there. If anyone wanted validation of what they were seeing from these three this season, this is probably it. It’s also evidenced in how the Flyers are playing this year compared to last. They are 12-10-3 for 27 points through 25 games; a year ago at this point, they were 13-10-2 for 28 points. Last year’s run to 25 games had fans smiling, as it represented a seven-point improvement from the year before. But deep down, it felt unsustainable. The Flyers seemed to be surviving off their penalty kill and their transition offense. They had nearly as many shorthanded goals (6) as they did power play goals (8). This year, it’s different. Not only does the current play seem sustainable, but it seems like it is trending upward. Philadelphia got to this point despite going 5-8-2 in the first 15 games. And a massive amount of that sentiment is thanks to the players that are headed to this tournament. Sanheim is perhaps the biggest component. “Surprise” probably isn’t the right word, but the level to which Sanheim’s taken his game is certainly nothing short of remarkable. He was almost traded in the summer of 2023, and last year’s Barry Ashbee Trophy-winning season was plenty good enough to make Flyers fans glad that trade never happened. This season has powered beyond that. He’s fourth in the NHL in average minutes at 25:30, ranks among the top 10 in the league in even strength points among defensemen at 14, and has been a factor in all three zones at all strengths for the Flyers this season. It's probably fair to say that Konecny has done what the Flyers had hoped he’d do this season, which was to build upon his All-Star season of a year ago. It might be considered remarkable that he’s done so to this extent, however. Konecny is currently on pace for a 40-goal, 100-point season. To put the significance of that in a bit of perspective, Konecny’s best point-per-game season so far in his career was 61 over 60 games in the 2022-23 season. Also consider that the Flyers have had one player record a 100+point season in the last 28 years, when Claude Giroux had 102 in the 2017-18 campaign. But it’s not just the point total, it’s the consistency with Konecny. He’s had at least a point in 17 of the Flyers’ 25 games this season; in the most recent 13, he’s had a point in 12 of them. He contributes at even strength (7-15-22), on the power play (5-2-7), and while he’s only scored one shorthanded goal this year, he’s probably been involved in close to double-digit shorthanded scoring chances. His 21:06 of ice time per game this year is almost three minutes more than any other Flyers forward, which includes averaging 3:00/game on the power play and 1:29/game on the penalty kill. It’s that versatility that will make him valuable to Team Canada’s roster. As for Ristolainen, he was long expected to be part of Team Finland as one of the top seven Finnish defensemen in the league. But even that squad will be getting an improved version of Ristolain

Option #2 – Pick Up at PPG Paints Arena Monday – Thursday Starting April 16 Through May 1 Fans may redeem their Jagr Bobblehead Vouchers in-person at PPG Paints Arena Monday through Thursday starting Tuesday, April 16, 2024 through Wednesday, May 1, 2024. Jagr Bobbleheads will be available for pick-up inside PPG Paints Arena’s Administrative Entrance located on Fifth Avenue (to the right of the Peoples Gate doors) from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM Monday through Thursday. Pick-up will only be available on non-event days. Vouchers will be scanned and collected inside the Administrative Entrance. Penguins Confirm Arrival of Jaromir Jagr Bobbleheads and Announce Distribution Dates as Soon as April 6 and 7 The Penguins have secured the truckload of stolen Jaromir Jagr bobbleheads and plan to begin distributing the promotional items at the team’s upcoming home game on Saturday, April 6, it was announced today by Penguins President of Business Operations Kevin Acklin. The Penguins were notified last week that a special cargo recovery team negotiated the return of the stolen property to a secure warehouse located in Ontario, California. The truckload arrived in Pittsburgh today and is expected to be delivered to PPG Paints Arena within the next week. The Jaromir Jagr bobbleheads are presented by Neighborhood Ford Store. Fans holding a bobblehead voucher from the March 14 game versus the San Jose Sharks will be able to begin redeeming their vouchers on Saturday, April 6 and Sunday, April 7. Details for both dates are below. Fans with tickets to the Saturday, April 6 game versus the Tampa Bay Lightning AND a Jagr bobblehead voucher will be able to redeem their vouchers inside PPG Paints Arena from the time doors open at 11:30 AM until 30 minutes following the conclusion of the game. Vouchers will be scanned and collected in the DICK’S Sporting Goods Wall of Champions Hallway, located behind Section 112, near the Ford Lounge. On Sunday, April 7, the Penguins will host a drive-thru pick-up option at PPG Paints Arena from 10:00 AM until 2:00 PM. Fans with Jagr bobblehead vouchers should remain in their vehicles and enter the Jim Shorkey Auto Group Garage located at 1300 Centre Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15219. Vouchers will be scanned and collected inside the garage prior to the bobbleheads being handed to fans. The website listed on the voucher is available by clicking here . This website includes the latest information and will continue to be updated with future redemption dates. A voucher from the original promotional date must be presented to redeem. Fans must present one voucher, per bobblehead. Fans with more than one Jagr bobblehead voucher may redeem all of their vouchers at one time. To read the original media release, please click here . title: Meet S. J. Sharkie | San Jose Sharks Official Mascot | San Jose Sharks
text: Follow Sharkie on Social X Facebook Instagram YouTube Sharkie Appearances Sharkie Gram Name In Lights FINatical Kids Club Video Shoutouts About S.J. Sharkie Since his NHL debut in January 1992, Sharkie has become one of the most recognized mascots in the sports world. He's a highly respected figure both inside and outside of the SAP Center and throughout the hockey community. A consistent and familiar presence at every Sharks home game, Sharkie has the enviable task of entertaining hockey fans night in and night out, performing a variety of humorous, exciting, death-defying, and unique stunts and acts. This loveable mascot makes a splash at more than 450 public appearances each year. Throughout his career, Sharkie's attended birthday parties to flower deliveries, bar mitzvahs to weddings, corporate events and charity fundraisers. He has escorted a high school student to her senior prom, acted as the ring bearer, best fish, and flower fish, and has walked brides down the aisle at wedding ceremonies. Aptly coined as "The Hardest Working Fish in Sports," Sharkie has been selected to represent the team at the NHL All-Star Game over 20 times and assisted in dropping the ceremonial first puck at the 1997 All-Star Game in San Jose. In 2012, the Cartoon Network selected him as the "Most Awesome Mascot" in all of sports at their Hall of Game Awards show, the first hockey mascot to win the award. Sharkie serves as the face of several Sharks community initiatives, including Reading Is Cool, Stick to Fitness, Anti-Bully Programming, Little Sharks, and the FINactical Kids Club. Besides his numerous public appearances, Sharkie is also involved with numerous Bay Area charities, and spending countless hours on behalf of the Sharks Foundation by lending a fin to their programs, fundraisers, meetings, and projects throughout the year (sharksfoundation.org). Sharkie's popularity has "spawned" his very own merchandise line and website, the first website ever devoted solely to a professional mascot . You can follow Sharkie on his very own social network pages as well ( Twitter: @sjsharkie , Facebook: sjsharkie , Instagram: @officialsjsharkie , Snapchat: @theSJSharkie and Tiktok: @theSJSharkie). Learn more about this fun-loving fish's appearance descriptions and opportunities for in-game events.

text: Crib Club Crib Club is exclusive club for all babies of Sharks Territory born at participating Kaiser Permanente delivery centers currently located at KP San Jose, KP Santa Clara, and KP Santa Cruz County. Learn More Sharks Foundation The Sharks Foundation is the official charitable arm of Sharks Sports & Entertainment and has donated more than $21 million to those in need since its inception in 1994. During the 2024-25 season, the Sharks Foundation provided nearly $1 million in support grants to Bay Area non-profit organizations. View the Sharks Foundation's 2023-24 Community Annual Report . Learn More School Programs The San Jose Sharks offer a variety of school programs such as reading, anti-bullying, financial education, STEM, and street hockey programs. Learn More Bay Area All-Star Scholarship Team Bay Area professional sports franchises have teamed up to form the Bay Area All-Star Scholarship Team (BAASST). Each sports team does its part in contributing to the BAASST program by identifying one outstanding student and awarding each of them a scholarship for $5,000. Learn More Stick To Fitness Stick to Fitness is a program dedicated to educating South Bay 4th-6th grade aged children on the importance of healthy living, while encouraging them to be active through on-site physical education instruction that continues at home. The program teaches lessons in health, fitness and hockey, all at no cost to the school / center. Stick To Fitness is available to schools, after school programs and community centers (YMCA, Boys and Girls Clubs). Learn More Little Sharks - "Learn to Play" The Little Sharks "Learn to Play" program is designed for children ages 4-8 who have no prior hockey experience and are interested in picking up the sport of ice hockey. Through fun, age-appropriate lessons, we hope to create a positive first-time hockey experience for our participants. Learn More San Jose Hockey Street Team The Sharks and Barracuda Street Team presented By Coca-Cola can bring their fun to your event. Opportunities could include a Slap Shot Inflatable, prize table and/or an interactive photo booth. These elements are a perfect addition to any festival, fair or community function. Learn More
